questions.question_text:
A netballer took $16$ shots at goal during a match and scored $14$ of them.
Express her scoring shots as a percentage.

options.why: Found the percentage of shots missed ($2$ out of $16$) instead of those scored.
Divided $14$ by $16$ correctly but did not multiply by $100$.
Expressed the remaining $78$ as a percentage of $130$ instead of the $52$.

questions.question_text:
A cyclist rode $84$ km on Sunday and $56$ km on Saturday.
Express Sunday's distance as a percentage of Saturday's.

options.why: Wrote $\dfrac{56}{84}$, comparing Saturday with Sunday instead.
Formed $\dfrac{84}{56}$ correctly but did not multiply by $100$.

questions.question_text:
A soccer squad has $25$ players, and $22$ of them attended training.
What percentage of the squad did not attend?

options.why: Found the percentage who did attend instead of those who did not.
Gave the number who missed training ($3$) as a percentage without dividing by $25$.

questions.question_text:
A training run is $12$ km long.
An athlete has run $3000$ m of it.
Express the distance run as a percentage of the whole run.

options.why: Used $\dfrac{3000}{12}$ without converting $12$ km to $12000$ m.
Inverted the fraction, comparing the whole run with the distance already run.

questions.question_text:
In a mixture, $40$ g of Chemical A is mixed with $85$ g of Chemical B.
What percentage of the mixture is Chemical A?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{40}{85}$, dividing by Chemical B alone instead of the whole mixture of $125$ g.
Found the percentage of Chemical B in the mixture rather than Chemical A.

questions.question_text:
Beth has £60.00.
She spends one quarter of her money.
How much does she have left?

options.why: Calculates the quarter spent rather than the amount left.
Increases the original amount instead of subtracting the spending.
Uses an incorrect fraction of the original £60.

questions.solution_text: One quarter of £60 is £15, so the amount left is £60-£15=£45.00.

questions.question_text:
A cup of flour is 350 grams.
What fraction of a 2.5 kg bag of flour is one cup in its simplest form?

options.why: Dividing grams by kilograms mixes units and does not form the required fraction.
This fraction is not in simplest form because both terms share a factor of 5.
The denominator has been reduced incorrectly, producing the wrong fraction value.

questions.solution_text: Convert 2.5 kg to 2500 g. The fraction is $\frac{350}{2500}$, which simplifies by dividing numerator and denominator by 50 to give $\frac{7}{50}$.
